rv.q: Lucie Jones is lovably goofy as Jenna, contrasted with David Hunter's world-weary Matty...
13 Going On 30 knows it’s a frosted cupcake of a musical, and it leans all the way in.
Andy Fickman’s production is utterly inoffensive – but it’s also hard to escape the feeling that this is really just intellectual property slop: formulaic and familiar.
The result is a limp copy-and-paste job that is neither nostalgic enough to satisfy those longing for the movie’s original sparkle nor bold enough to justify itself as something new.
Overall, the production is a triumph, ending with a huge standing ovation.
With strong central performances and a nostalgic heart, it feels like a production that could grow into a sparkling addition to the stage musical canon.
13 Going On 30 the Musical is a joyous, feel good musical.
It’s not the next great musical but it’s got a real charm to it which won me over.

cn.t: Mixed reviews greet this rom-com adaptation: fans praise Lucie Jones's charming lead performance and energetic choreography, but critics are divided, with some finding it nostalgic fun and others dismissing it as bland and underpowered.

vr.q: I just think that if you're expecting something of a quality resembling some other film-to-stage adaptations like a Mean Girls, like a Legally Blonde, like a Heathers, then you're not really getting that from this score and from this writing and from this production.
